display.title: Mincha on the Rooftop: The Brother Who Visited New York
display.summary_short: A rich man in New York proudly shows his poor brother from the shtetl his many rooms and the view from his skyscraper roof, and finds him quietly davening Mincha in a corner.
display.summary_long: The Rebbe told this story in the name of the Frierdiker Rebbe. Two poor brothers shared a single room in a little shtetl in Europe. One moved to America, became very rich, and wanted to show his brother how well he had done, so he sent him a ticket. The brother in Europe was content at home, but he needed money to marry off his daughters, so he made the trip, planning to let his brother show him around before asking for help. The rich brother led him through room after room, a room for eating, for drinking, for sleeping, for receiving guests, and when that did not impress him, took him up to the roof of a tall building to show him New York in every direction. Suddenly he noticed he was running around alone: his brother was in a corner davening Mincha. Asked why he could not wait, the visitor said he could not understand how anyone could live among so many distractions, so he used the time to daven. The Rebbe's lesson: everything Hashem gives us is for serving Him, and when it is time to daven, learn or give tzedakah, we stop everything.
display.lesson: Everything Hashem gives us is meant for serving Him; when it is time to daven, learn Torah or give tzedakah, we stop everything else and turn the physical into something holy.

characters: the poor brother from the shtetl

sources_cited.note: The Rebbe told the story in the name of the Frierdiker Rebbe and drew the lesson.

quality.notes: Filename 'pizur hanefesh' = a scattered, distracted soul. The narrator once says 'shtetl in which he lived in New York' (slip for Europe).
